results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records; and b. Record those time stamps for audit records such that the time stamps meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both retrieved CloudTrail audit records for the churn-predictor-endpoint carry timestamps that conform to AU-8 requirements. Specifically: (1) Timestamps are generated by AWS internal system clocks (satisfying AU-8.a). (2) Both timestamps — "2025-12-01T11:00:00Z" (CreateEndpoint, evidence ccdb2710) and "2026-03-15T14:22:00Z" (UpdateEndpoint, evidence 03b60152) — are in ISO 8601 format with the "Z" (Zulu/UTC) suffix, satisfying the UTC requirement of AU-8.b. (3) Granularity is to the second (HH:MM:SS), which meets standard organizational granularity expectations. Confidence is medium rather than high because only two audit events were available for review, and the organization's formally defined granularity requirement was not retrievable from the evidence — if sub-second precision were required, this could not be confirmed. The change-control anomalies noted in the event metadata are relevant to other controls (e.g., CM-3, SA-10) but do not affect AU-8 conformance.
gaps: Only two CloudTrail events were available; a broader audit log sample would increase confidence.

The organization's formally defined granularity of time measurement (AU-8 Assignment parameter) was not available in the retrieved evidence — sub-second precision requirements cannot be confirmed or denied.
No evidence was available confirming NTP/time-source configuration for the underlying compute infrastructure (would further substantiate AU-8.a compliance).
